route.name: error-routing

note.lineText: // The M060 SC6 surface, whose one line the dead-click note above it pays for by its own fold: the message and the code an uncaught error's own text carried, the owner the arrival's own field named or `owner-not-in-the-message`, the phase the records decided or `phase-not-recorded`, and each absence of the join as its own line — or the cannot-tell state that names what the records did not carry, with no remedy, no cause and no handler identity the answer did not state.

route.statement: one entry of the `PANEL_SURFACES` list, spread into the `appRoutes` table by the one mapped literal the table ends with, lazy through the shared `loadPanelDemo` closure the table defines once, and naming its surface in `data.surface` as every demo-backed route does. It sits between `interaction-story` and `dead-click` rather than after `what-changed`, for the reason the list’s own note states: the `m048`/`m049`/`m050` route records cite the loader’s two lines (14–15), the `copy-check` (97), `interaction-story` (103) and `dead-click` (110) path lines and the declaration and mapped-literal lines below the list (113, 146, 147), so the entry’s one line is paid for by folding two lines of the M050 note into their neighbours’ text and every line those records cite keeps its number. The route registers nothing and measures nothing at render time: it reaches the pane that renders the join’s answer.

loader.statement: the `error-routing` key is one entry of the `LOADERS` map and it is the only path to `panel-error-routing.ts`: the demo looks the key up by the name the route’s `data.surface` states, awaits the dynamic import, calls the module’s default export with the sample fact, and sets the state and the lines the module answers. The key cost one line, and that line sits inside the `LOADERS` map above the component, where the M060 pane module is new and no surface record had cited the map’s entries by line; the loader resolution block (717, 723–726), the component template and every earlier fact keep their numbers because the one line the map gained was paid for by folding one comment line of the `fields` fact into its neighbour. The fact is the join’s own answer over a record written in the shape T001 measured: `state: uncaught-with-handler`, the message the arrival’s own payload carries, the code that message’s own text carries, `owner: null` (the arrival carries no `component`), the phase absence, one absence, three claims each carrying its artefact path and the handler state in the join’s own detail — and `panel-demo.spec.ts` rebuilds that record from the shipped record-shapes measurement, evaluates the shipped join from its committed text and holds this fact to that answer field for field.

answer.statement: the join answers `{ state, message, code, owner, phase, absences, claims, detail }` with every field in every state. The demo’s sample is the `uncaught-with-handler` answer: the message the arrival’s own payload carries, the NG0NNN code that message’s own text carries, no owner (the arrival records no `component`), the phase absence no record in this tree displaces, `phase-not-recorded` beside no other absence, one claim per record the answer cites with the path that record carries, and the join’s own detail sentence — which names the handler state the handler record itself carries and nothing beside it. The message texts and the handler name are fixture data: T001 measured the payload shape (`{code, message, component, timestamp}`), the two record paths the claims cite and the phase absence, never a page’s message or a handler class.

cannotTellAnswer.statement: `cannot-tell` is the join’s own answer to `{}`: the records do not name the inputs it reads, so nothing is decided. The pane renders the state, the shared `no-reason` sentence the copy digest carries, the phase line, the absence line and the join’s `detail`, and no message, code or owner value, because the answer carries none of the three.

No browser was opened, no page was read, no profiler was tapped and no build was run.

No page read produced this answer and none could: the message texts and the handler name are fixture data. T001 measured the payload shape the listeners reduce an arrival to, the two record paths the claims cite and the phase absence (count 2), never a page’s message or a handler class. The milestone’s answer is the join’s own over a record written in that measured shape, and the demo’s spec re-derives it on every test run.

The record does not measure what the pane looks like. The one sentence it renders is enumerated in `panel-error-routing.ts`’s `PANE_SENTENCES` and is explained by a row `extension/copy-digest.json` already carries under the surface `components` — the shared `no-reason` text, which no new digest row was needed for; this record names the states and the field each reads rather than reproducing the rendering.

The record does not claim the copy record was re-measured by this task’s first pass alone. `research/raw/m048-surface-copy.json` stated 30 surfaces and 212 sentences and did not carry `panel-error-routing.ts`; the same task re-measured it over the thirty-first surface — its one registry sentence (the shared `no-reason` text the digest already carries) and its one inline label — so that record now states 31 surfaces and 213 sentences, `scripts/copy-check.test.mjs` is green at 30 of 30, and the `copyRecordSurfaces` and `copyRecordSentencesCompared` counts above are the re-measured record’s.
verdict: measured: the panel route `error-routing` is one lazy route — a `PANEL_SURFACES` entry spread into `appRoutes` by the one mapped literal, sitting between `interaction-story` and `dead-click` and costing the list one line that the M050 note’s own fold pays for, so no line the route records cite moves — whose `data.surface` names the `error-routing` key of `panel-demo.ts`’s `LOADERS`, and that key is the only path to `panel-error-routing.ts`. The pane renders the join’s four states and nothing it did not state: the finding names the message and the code the message’s own text carries and the owner only where a field of the arrival names one — the owner line carrying `owner-not-in-the-message` where it names none — `reached-handler` renders the same fields with the join’s own `no finding` detail and never a clean page, `no-handler-provided` names no handler identity the object did not carry, and `cannot-tell` renders the shared `no-reason` sentence, the phase and the absences and the detail with no message, code or owner value. The phase line is never blank: it carries whichever word the join returned, and no record in this tree displaces the absence. The pane names no cause, no remedy and no schematic, because the answer carries none. The panel carries 30 surfaces and 30 loader keys, the route table 39 ordered paths, and `extension/copy-digest.json` 204 rows — none of them this pane’s, because its one sentence is the shared `no-reason` text the digest already holds under `components`.
